invention.author_prose:
In the hotel suite bedroom, the wearer says only that they are doing a quick checkout reset: clear the desk, return the hand towel to the bathroom shelf, and wipe the bathroom shelf and the desk before leaving. The glasses can see three loose things on the bedroom desk at the start: a mug, the wearer’s cell phone, and a sponge. The desk is the surface that will be wiped, so “clear the desk” means the mug and phone must not still be on it when the wiping starts.

The wearer first takes the mug from the desk and puts it on the bedroom shelf. The assistant says nothing, because that is a valid part of clearing the desk. The wearer then takes the hand towel, walks into bathroom_0, puts the towel on a bathroom shelf, uses it to wipe that shelf, and briefly looks over the other bathroom shelf area. These bathroom actions are useful and consistent with the stated reset; the assistant should remain silent rather than nagging while the wearer is still working through the job.

The wearer walks back into bedroom_0 and turns toward the desk with the sponge still lying there. The live camera view now shows the cell phone still on the desk, and the action history shows that only the mug was moved off the desk. No wrong action has happened yet, but the next intended transition is clearly the desk-wiping step. At that moment the strong assistant intervenes once: “Hold on—the phone is still on the desk. Move it to the bedroom shelf before you wipe the desk.”

In the corrected branch, the wearer takes the phone from the desk, puts it on the bedroom shelf beside the mug, and then wipes the desk with the sponge. Success is visible and scorable because the mug and phone end up on the bedroom shelf, the hand towel is on the bathroom shelf, and the wipe happens only after the desk has been cleared.

A weak always-silent assistant lets the wearer wipe the desk while the phone remains on it. A weak overactive assistant that speaks during the earlier mug or bathroom steps is also poorly timed, because those actions are not omissions. The diagnostic error is specifically failing to notice the missing desk-clearing step just before the wipe makes it consequential.

capability.boundary: No wrong action has occurred yet. The evidence is the missing prerequisite, so an object-identity mix-up is not sufficient.
capability.few_shot: A photographer is packing a camera body and spare battery into a hard equipment case. The wearer completes both placements and reaches to close the case, but the observed prefix never includes the memory card still lying on the desk. The assistant stays silent through the correct placements and intervenes before the close action, directing the wearer to put the card inside and then close the case. The missing action is recoverable from the opening trace; the default branch closes an incomplete case, while the corrected branch ends with all three items inside and the case closed.
capability.target: Infer that a required action is absent from the completed prefix and intervene before a later transition makes the omission consequential.
